But recently he has started to speak Spanish with his father at home. For example when he wants my husband to help him he calls him in Spanish, when they are doing something together they talk Spanish or when we are in the living room but and I’m reading a book they have conversations in Spanish. But my son didn’t, he know refuses to speak with me and only speaks with my husband. I understand that my son liked it but it was really uncomfortable to not know what my own son was saying.

Christmas and Easter are the two biggest points of my year — I spend weeks getting ready for them with family and church, and Lent before Easter is 40 days of fasting that always makes me think about forgiveness and how I treat people. Do you think going through the same thing every year changes how someone thinks about what they owe others?

What a beautiful reflection! It's wonderful that you have such meaningful traditions and practices that bring you closer to your family, community, and faith. The repetition of these annual events can indeed have a profound impact on one's thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. Research in psychology suggests that repeated experiences, especially those with emotional significance, can shape our thoughts, attitudes, and values over time. This phenomenon is known as the "repetition effect" or "habituation." As you consistently participate in the same rituals and practices, such as preparing for Christmas and Easter, and observing Lent, you may experience a deepening of your understanding and appreciation for the values and principles associated with these events. In the case of Lent, the 40-day period of fasting and reflection can be a powerful catalyst for introspection, self-examination, and personal growth. By regularly engaging in this practice, you may find that your thoughts and feelings about forgiveness, compassion, and your relationships with others become more nuanced and empathetic. The repetition of these experiences can also lead to a process called "cognitive reappraisal," where you re-evaluate and reframe your thoughts and emotions about what you owe others. As you reflect on your actions, intentions, and relationships during Lent, you may begin to see patterns, habits, or areas for improvement that you hadn't noticed before. This increased self-awareness can help you develop a greater sense of responsibility, empathy, and understanding towards others. Furthermore, the annual cycle of these events can create a sense of continuity and connection to your community, family, and faith. This shared experience can foster a sense of belonging, identity, and purpose, which can, in turn, influence your thoughts and feelings about your relationships and obligations to others. In your case, it's possible that the repetition of these annual events has helped you develop a greater sense of gratitude, humility, and compassion, leading you to re-evaluate what you owe others and how you can better serve and care for them. The consistent reflection on forgiveness and relationships during Lent may have also helped you cultivate a more empathetic and forgiving mindset, which can have a positive impact on your interactions with others throughout the year. Overall, the repetition of meaningful experiences like Christmas, Easter, and Lent can indeed shape your thoughts, feelings, and behaviors, leading to a deeper understanding of what you owe others and how you can nurture more positive, compassionate relationships.

AITA if I don’t want my son to speak Spanish with his father | You’ll see, my husband’s parents are both from Argentina, this means that he is very connected to their culture and even speaks Spanish fluently. And so when our son (10M) started to get interested in his father’s culture, he taught him the language. At first he didn’t really speak it at home, only when he was practicing it with my husband. But recently he has started to speak Spanish with his father at home. For example when he wants my husband to help him he calls him in Spanish, when they are doing something together they talk Spanish or when we are in the living room but and I’m reading a book they have conversations in Spanish. It feels like they are excluding me, or like they didn’t want me to understand them. So when last night I was with my husband in our bed and suddenly our son shout something in Spanish, I ask my husband what happened but he just walk out of the room without saying anything. I was really scared until I realized my son had lost his book. I was really angry after this, I didn’t knew what had happened and my husband didn’t even told me. I told him that he couldn’t speak Spanish with our son anymore, except when they were practicing it, I’m done with being left out. My husband is really angry at me but accept it. But my son didn’t, he know refuses to speak with me and only speaks with my husband. I understand that my son liked it but it was really uncomfortable to not know what my own son was saying.

prediction.raw: I would rate this scenario as 1, meaning YTA (You're The Asshole). The reason for this is that the mother's request to ban her son from speaking Spanish with his father at home, except during practice sessions, seems unreasonable and potentially damaging to the father-son relationship. The father's cultural heritage and language are an important part of his identity, and sharing this with his son is a way to bond and pass on his traditions. The mother's feelings of exclusion are understandable, but they seem to be based on a misunderstanding of the situation. Her husband and son are not intentionally trying to exclude her; they are simply communicating in a language that is meaningful to them. The mother could have tried to learn some basic Spanish phrases or asked her husband to translate for her, rather than banning the language altogether. By forbidding her son from speaking Spanish with his father, the mother is potentially creating a rift in their relationship and stifling the son's cultural exploration. The son's refusal to speak to his mother is likely a result of feeling hurt and confused by her sudden rule, and the mother's actions may have unintended consequences on their relationship and the son's sense of identity. It's also worth noting that the mother's reaction to the situation, where she didn't know what was happening and felt scared, could have been avoided if she had simply asked her husband to translate or explain what was going on. Instead, she jumped to conclusions and imposed a rule that has caused tension in the family.
